## TL;DR

Running board and pipeline cards no longer append noisy “active N ago” or elapsed-time suffixes on the status line. Recency moves into the existing `data-tip` hover/focus popover via a small `card-activity-recency` helper. Silent/stuck labels stay inline. Unit and component tests cover the new behaviour; scoped `repoos check` is the handoff gate.

## Work and rationale

The human report called out cards like #1057 and #1055 where a healthy engineer session showed “CONFIRMING HANDOFF · ACTIVE JUST NOW” or “CODING · ACTIVE 1M AGO”. That text almost always reads as “just now” and forces a second line on the chip, while the meaningful signal is prolonged silence (“SILENT 6M”, “STUCK”).

The fix keeps labels short and pushes last-activity timing to the styled tooltip stack the board already uses (`data-tip` on `.tc-hint`, not native `title`). A dedicated module centralises formatting so TaskCard, auto-repair retry hints, integrating close-out copy, and PipelineCard share one vocabulary.

## Approaches tried

The first change point was `resolveActiveEngineerCardHint` in `src/core/active-task-card.ts`, which had been appending `coding · active ${duration} ago`. That suffix was removed so the default running label is simply `coding`, matching #1000’s richer states (checks, queues) which already encode timing only when something is wrong.

`TaskCard.vue` gained an optional `activityTip` on `CardHint`. For `tc-coding` hints, `agentLastActivityTip` builds “Active 3m ago” plus a full local timestamp from the same `formatActivity` helper the old inline suffix used. The hint’s `data-tip` is merged via `cardHintDataTip(title, activityTip)` so hover still shows the explanatory paragraph below the recency lines.

Auto-repair paths (`confirming handoff`, `fixing check failure`, `fixing merge conflict`) followed the same pattern: `retryHint` drops `· active …` from the visible label and sets `activityTip` when activity is known. Integrating close-out copy in `integration-pipeline-ui.ts` drops elapsed minutes from the chip and exposes `elapsedTip` for the popover unless the job is stalled (stalled copy still belongs on the line).

`PipelineCard.vue` hides the right-hand elapsed span when `state === "ok"` and attaches `stateElapsedTip` to `.pl-step` with `tabindex="0"` for keyboard access. Stuck and other non-ok states keep elapsed visible inline because duration there is part of the alert.

## Challenges and blockers

Coordinating with #1057 was noted in the task; this branch builds on the landed `activeEngineerCardHint` path rather than duplicating status derivation. Ensuring every hint source fed `activityTip` required tracing the hint `computed` chain: `codingOrStuckHint` and integration `copy.elapsedTip` were wired; `autoRepairHint` returns `RetryHint` shapes that already include `activityTip` and are compatible with `CardHint`.

Shot capture needs the existing `board:activeCoding` fixture (#9999) so selectors stay unique on a busy preview board. Popover visibility in PNG captures depends on a hover step on the hint trigger. The `closeOut:remoteTests` shot-fixture test was updated in this session because integrating labels no longer embed elapsed minutes inline.

## Key learnings

Keeping recency out of the line is a presentation choice, not a data-model change: the board still tracks `agentActivityAt` and the same silence thresholds drive stuck labelling. Centralising popover copy in `card-activity-recency.ts` avoids three divergent string builders and makes table-driven tests cheap. Pipeline “ok” rows treat elapsed as metadata like healthy engineer activity—visible on demand, not in the primary scan line.
